q: How do I count makeready paper waste in a print job's footprint?
title: Print jobs: makeready waste
short: Charge each job with the paper it actually consumed, good sheets plus makeready and spoilage. Use the press log for sheets run, multiply by sheet weight, and apply the paper factor to the total, not just to the delivered copies.
audience: Commercial offset and packaging printers quoting a per job or per copy carbon figure

ol: Sheets fed for the job, including makeready, from the press counter or job ticket.
Sheet weight from size and grammage.
Tonnes times the paper factor per tonne, plus the job's share of press energy.

p: Short runs carry more waste per copy. A figure that ignores makeready understates short jobs and makes long runs look worse by comparison.
Selling trimmings and spoilage to a recycler does not reduce the job's paper use; it is reported separately, in category 5 only for disposal you pay for.
